name: t23-g4-join-budget
description: T23 / G4 row 11 join budget, worst-case-sized evidence -- currently an accurate FAILING repro, not a passing gate; see docs/reports/G3.md row 11 for the full writeup. Same eight-client g4-workload scene/population/cuts as t23-g4-workload (256 active + 4096 sleeping bodies = 4352 bodies, two multi-region column cuts, a round-robined edit stream, two blasts) -- t23-g4-workload's own increment-19 run already measured this population's late-join baseline at 48,122 compressed bytes per client with no network shaping (ready in 22.7-25.8 s purely from 8-way CPU capture contention on the tick thread). This fixture adds the missing piece: client 7's connection is shaped to the exact docs/validation.md G3 join-budget network profile (1 MiB/s bandwidth, 100 ms RTT, 20 ms jitter, 2% packet loss) via the `join_budget` block, while clients 0-6 stay on transparent proxies so the population/edit workload itself is not bandwidth-limited. Client 7's own background baseline-capture thread has to contend with the other seven's simultaneous capture threads for real CPU time; that contention alone (proven by t23-g4-workload, no shaping involved) already costs 20-25 s, and client 7's connection hits the transport's 30 s QUIC idle timeout while still waiting on its own capture, before the server ever sends it a BaselineBegin -- `result: "join-failed"`, not a measured budget. This is a real, reproducible gap (see docs/reports/G3.md row 11), not a fixture bug: it shows the current implementation cannot serve a worst-case-sized dependency-complete baseline to a network-constrained client while seven other simultaneous joiners are also capturing. `restart_check` is intentionally omitted (t23-g4-workload already covers cold-restart recovery for this scene; this fixture's only new work is the join-budget measurement, and dropping it keeps this run's already-long release-profile duration bounded).
